heroLead: Star Junction grew up as a coal patch town near Perryopolis, the kind of place where a family's mineral history is often older and stranger than anyone still living remembers.
intro: Star Junction sits in Fayette County near Perryopolis, along the Youghiogheny River corridor, and like a lot of the small patch towns in this part of the county, its history runs through coal company land ownership more than family farming. Mineral deeds here can carry reservations dating back over a century, sometimes with coal, oil, and gas severed at different times by different companies, which makes tracing exact ownership a genuine research project.

The wet-gas Marcellus window covers this part of Fayette County, and modern drilling units have, in places, ended up overlapping with these old coal-company-era mineral splits, creating layered ownership that takes patience to sort through correctly.

sections.heading: When Coal Company History Complicates a Gas Deed
paragraphs: If a coal company severed and later sold off oil and gas rights separately from the coal itself, your current interest might trace through several corporate transfers before landing with your family. We do the legwork to trace that chain accurately rather than assuming a simple, clean history that isn't there.

sections.heading: Getting to a Real Number
paragraphs: Once we've confirmed exactly what your deed grants and whether your tract sits inside an active or planned unit, we build an offer around actual production data where it exists, or reasonable development likelihood where it doesn't. We explain every part of that math so you're not signing on faith.

faqs.question: My deed mentions a coal company I've never heard of. Does that matter?
faqs.answer: It might. Many Fayette County coal companies severed and sold oil and gas rights separately over the decades, and tracing that history is part of confirming exactly what you own today.

faqs.question: Is Star Junction inside an active Marcellus unit?
faqs.answer: It depends on the specific parcel. We check current DEP permit and unit data against your exact tract before estimating any value.

faqs.question: What paperwork do I need to get started?
faqs.answer: A copy of your deed is the best starting point. If you have a lease, division order, or old probate paperwork, that helps too, but we can often locate what's missing at the recorder of deeds office.

faqs.question: How long does it usually take to trace a coal-company-era chain of title?
faqs.answer: It depends on how many transfers your interest has passed through. Some Star Junction tracts take a few days to confirm, while others with several corporate transactions can take a couple of weeks. We handle that research at no cost to you before making an offer.
